fair_value_reason: 50/50 blend. (1) EV/EBITDA: NTM-at-horizon EBITDA $8.6B (between the 0.25 x 2027 + 0.75 x 2028 consensus of $8.33B and agents' $8.5-9.0B, given the strip above consensus) x 8.5x (the ex-majors NTM median; +17% to the 7.3x core median for contracted growth) = EV $73.1B, less net debt ~$46.0B, less NCI $3.5B (it includes the VGLNG preferred), less ~$1.6B after-tax expected BP award, over 2.58B diluted shares = $8.53. (2) P/E: NTM-at-horizon EPS $1.30 x 11.0x (-12% to the 12.5x NTM peer median), less $0.62/share BP = $13.68. The blend is $11.10, against the agent mean of $12.10. The difference is almost entirely the EV/EBITDA multiple (8.5x vs the 8.75-9.25x agents used) plus the net-debt path.
supervisor_summary: The round-2 forecasts converged on the round-1 fixes (uncapped BP, NCI in the bridge, $13.13 close, NTM-at-horizon basis), and the mean fair value fell from $13.0 to $12.1. One shared error remained: every agent framed its ~9x EV/EBITDA as a discount to trailing peer multiples. On one consistent NTM basis, the core LNG/energy median is 7.3x and VG already trades at 9.5x. Applying 8.5x with consensus net debt gives a reconciled fair value of ~$11.1, below the $13.13 close, so my ladder sits ~3 points below the agent mean near the money (median ~$12.05). The 9 Nov Q3 disclosure of 2027 forward sales and Hormuz timing remain the big swing factors; the thesis break stays at $8.
key_drivers: 2027 open position: $650-700M of 2027 EBITDA per $1/MMBtu (Q2-26 call). The 9 Nov Q3 disclosure of how much is already sold forward is the single largest swing.
Hormuz/Qatar timing: Qatar force majeure runs to early November; deep markets put a reopening by 31 Dec at ~20% and by mid-2027 at ~45% (Kalshi). A reopening roughly halves the open-cargo fee.
Multiple on a consistent NTM basis: the core LNG/energy peer median is 7.3x EV/EBITDA (LNG-pure 10.3x); VG trades at 9.5x NTM today. I give a justified multiple of 8.5x, not 9.0x.

Leverage and claims ahead of equity: consensus net debt rises to $47.7B (2027) and $52.6B (2028); NCI is $3.5B; the uncapped BP award (hearing May 2027) has an expected cost of ~$2B pre-tax. Each 1x of EV/EBITDA is ~$3.3/share.
Consensus EBITDA: 2026 $8.94B, 2027 $7.24B, 2028 $8.69B. The 2028 rebound (Plaquemines Ph2, CP2) is what justifies a premium over the integrated majors.
